samples.question: On the left is a round dial with a dark grey hub at its centre and one red arrow drawn outward from that hub. The arrow is drawn close to one of the four directions up, right, down or left; its heading is whichever of those four is nearest to the way it is drawn. To the right of the dial is a row of cream cards, each carrying a single straight blue bar through its centre. Each blue bar is drawn close to one of four orientations: horizontal, rising to the right at 45 degrees, vertical, or falling to the right at 45 degrees; a bar's orientation is whichever of those four is nearest to the way it is drawn. Each card is a mirror: applying a card reflects the arrow's current heading in the line of that card's blue bar, so a heading already lying along the bar is unchanged, a heading perpendicular to the bar is reversed, and in general a heading at angle a to the bar comes back at angle a on the other side of the bar. The cards are applied one at a time, in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below the row shows. The dial is drawn only in its starting state: no later heading, and not the final heading, is drawn anywhere in the picture. Reflecting a heading that points up, right, down or left in any of the four bar orientations always gives another heading that points up, right, down or left. After every card has been applied in order, which way does the arrow point? Answer with one word: up, right, down or left.
